title: AI-Powered Assistance in Formulating Research Questions
summary: A plain-language paper, reusable prompt and journal-credibility rubric on how AI can help researchers form answerable research questions, and the guardrails that use requires.

contribution.roleNote: Masters research by an Ethical Tech CoLab student cohort at the NYU Center for Global Affairs; Yorke is listed among the authors.

narrative.problem: AI is increasingly used to help academic researchers pose research questions by mining large literatures, but the same tools can hallucinate citations, fabricate conceptual linkages, overstate consensus and shift a researcher's framing toward what the model predicts rather than what the literature supports.
narrative.decision: Pairs AI for ideation with AI for critical interrogation: a reusable researcher prompt that scores sources against a fixed journal-credibility rubric, plus a proposed red-team agent that audits citations and flags unsupported claims.
narrative.tradeoff: The guidance is model-agnostic text rather than software, so nothing enforces it: its value depends on researchers independently checking sources, and the red-team agent remains a proposal.
narrative.limitation: The prompt is unevaluated. Peer review recommended major revisions and found every effect claim is design argument; a minimal evaluation protocol is sketched but has not been run, and the planned Next.js application is not built.
narrative.caveat: The paper was partly generated and checked with the M365 Copilot Researcher Agent running OpenAI GPT v5; treat AI-suggested research questions as exploratory starting points, not conclusions.
